title: Estimating the Minimum Oracle-Relative Loss of Harm-Averse Treatment Lotteries
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field (target=field) and NOT salvageable in scope; mathematical referee PASS and independent MAIN validity confirms downgraded bank.
gap_reasons: The delivered result is a two-sided log-log bracket; exact minimax logarithms, log-log necessity and exact risk-length equivalence remain unresolved, consistently with the framing.
Known uniform covariates, fair randomized treatment and known smoothness restrict the delivered inference result, leaving the observational RHC setting outside its application domain.

The conservative certificate can equal the entire target range at practical sample sizes, while efficient implementation and evidence of informative finite-sample intervals are absent; these practical limits and the remaining logarithmic gap constrain the projected leading-econometrics paper score.
proof_attempt_summary: The proposal passed D-0.5 and D0 discharged its informal theorem graph after a constructed-object repair, including public tuning and all-n upper assembly. D0.5 mathematical review passed, but general review assessed subfield novelty below the fixed field floor (score ceiling 6.5 versus 7.4); independent boundary and MAIN validity consultations found no bounded in-scope tier-lifting repair. Exact logarithms, log-log necessity and exact risk/length equivalence remain open.
tldr: The smallest worst-case oracle-relative loss of a harm-averse treatment lottery is an identified nonsmooth scalar of two conditional arm means. On the entire fixed Hölder class in an original randomized Bernoulli experiment, the target is a finite-sample bracket for absolute estimation risk and honest connected expected interval length: both lie between \(r_-(n)\) and \(r_+(n)=r_-(n)\log\log(e^e n)\), up to public-class constants. A coarse pilot and finer spatial cells must jointly deliver a computable tensor-polynomial estimator and its public error certificate. Supported original-law mixtures must deliver the two lower bounds separately. Population lottery balancing, polynomial moments, fuzzy hypotheses, and Markov calibration are credited; exact logarithms remain outside the theorem contract.
gap: Population randomized ambiguity decisions do not determine how precisely their minimum loss can be estimated. The closest scalar nonsmooth-functional results leave a Hölder endpoint gap, while regular optimal-value inference excludes parts of the present full class through separation and first-stage conditions.
fill: The certificate synthesis task joins one finite tensor polynomial to count-conditioned original Bernoulli moments, all observed-count fallbacks, and a public finite-sample error bound. Same-class supported priors and coverage-event transfer give separate absolute-risk and connected-length converses.
